To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATP and its structural derivatives evoke currents in rat microglial purinoreceptors, which are non selective cation channels, and potassium channels.
ATP and its structural analogue, 2 methylthiol ATP induce an inward current in microglial cells.
ATP and its structural derivatives induce an inwardly rectifying current that can be either inward or outward, depending on the membrane potential of rat microglia in culture.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of ATP receptors in rat microglial cell lines.
the characterization of the purinergic receptors in rat microglial cell culture.
the electrophysiological characterization of the purinoceptor subtypes present in activated microglia, and their possible function in the modulation of the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ATP induced current is a mixture of a cationic current, which depolarizes the cell membrane, and a potassium current, which hyperpolarizes the membrane.
microglia possess two types of purinoceptors, the P2X and the P2Y, and that these purinoceptors are differentially regulated by the proliferative state of these cells.
the ATP induced currents in rat microglia are mediated by P2Y receptors and that these receptors may play a role in microglial proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ATP and its analogues are involved in cell activation and proliferation of microglia.
ATP induces depolarization and activation of microglial cells.
ATP and its analogues can depolarize microglial cells by activating cationic channels, which are present both in proliferating (resting) and non proliferating (activated) cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP is an important modulator of the resting membrane potential of microglia.
microglial cells are a heterogeneous population, which is not only reflected by their proliferative state, but also by the expression and function of different ion channels.
microglial cells have two different membrane potential states.
